extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards for when a patent application is considered abandoned, how express abandonment is validly made, examiner handling of abandonment, and the requirements and evidentiary/showing standards for petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment or to revive an abandoned application under 37 CFR §§1.135, 1.137, 1.138 and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §§1.134 and 1.136, the application becomes abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution to save an application must include a complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require. An amendment filed after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application from abandonment. Examiners should notify applicant of abandonment using form PTOL-1432 when appropriate and should not enter late amendments that arrive after the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and proper reply requirement to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid abandonment, the applicant must file such complete and proper reply as the condition of the application requires within the statutory (or properly extended) period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply that is nonresponsive to the last Office action, or an amendment after final that is improper, will not save the case. If a reply is a bona fide attempt and substantially complete but inadvertently omits some matter, applicant may be given a new time under §1.134 to supply the omission (see MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment formalities (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: Express abandonment requires filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application and signed by the applicant and the assignee of record, if any, or by the attorney or agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered attorney or agent acting under §1.34(a) may expressly abandon a prior application only when filing a continuing application. An express abandonment is not recognized unless actually received by appropriate officials in time to act before the date of issue. The letter must properly identify the application and be correctly signed; otherwise it is not a proper express abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may validly sign an express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An express abandonment must be signed by the applicant (acquiesced in by assignee if there is one), by the assignee through an officer whose position is indicated, or by the attorney/agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the exception of express abandonments resulting from filing a continuing/CPA under §1.53(d) or former §1.62, all express abandonments must be signed by all inventors, the owners of the entire interest, or an attorney/agent of record. The provisions of §1.34 do not apply unless filed with a continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectivity and dating of an express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An expressed abandonment becomes effective when an appropriate Office official takes action recognizing it; the date of abandonment may be the date of recognition or another date specified in the letter (e.g., as of the filing date of a continuing application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: where a continuing application requests abandonment of the prior application as of the continuing application's filing date, the prior application's abandonment date will be in accordance with that request once recognized. Examiner/Pub.Div. acknowledgments are used to recognize compliance with §1.138.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: When an express abandonment letter complying with §1.138 is received, the examiner should acknowledge receipt (e.g., form paragraph 7.88). If the letter does not comply, send an explanatory letter and use Notice of Abandonment form PTO-1432 as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.88 may be used to acknowledge proper express abandonments. If noncompliant, use form paragraph 7.89 to explain why the letter fails to comply (for example, signer not of record). Letters not timely filed (outside the period for reply) should be endorsed on the file but not formally entered and the application pulled for abandonment after minimum reply period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on withdrawal of an allowed application (37 CFR 1.313)
rubrics_metrics.description: An allowed application will not be withdrawn from issue except by approval of the Commissioner, and after payment of the issue fee will not be withdrawn for any reason except specified grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible grounds to withdraw an allowed application include (A) Office mistake, (B) violation of §1.56 or illegality, (C) unpatentability of one or more claims, (D) interference, or (E) abandonment to permit consideration of an IDS in a continuing application. Where §1.313 precludes giving effect to an express abandonment, remedy is a petition under §1.183.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment canceling all claims is not express abandonment (Ex parte Lasscell)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the filing date of an application that cancels all claims, even if signed by applicant and assignee, is not an express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment is regarded as nonresponsive and should not be entered; it does not operate as an express abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment by withdrawal or failure to prosecute appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may become abandoned through withdrawal of, or failure to prosecute, an appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences or dismissal of an appeal to the Federal Circuit where no amendment putting the case in condition for issue was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§1215–1216. Abandonment also results from failure to perfect an appeal as required by the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to take required action during statutory period (insufficiency and lateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment can result either from failure to reply within the statutory period or from an insufficient reply (failure to file a complete and proper reply within the statutory period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment is filed after the statutory period it is treated as late, the application is abandoned, late amendment is endorsed but not entered, and the examiner should notify applicant (PTOL-1432). Use form paragraph 7.90 or 7.91 for standard notices. Examiner must know the precise commencement and expiration dates of the statutory period including any extensions under §1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply—examples and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply within the period may nonetheless be insufficient if it is not fully responsive to the Office action (e.g., copying claims from a patent when not suggested by the Office does not constitute a response to the last Office action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply appears to be bona fide with inadvertent omission, use different form paragraph (e.g., 7.95). If reply not fully responsive and period expired, issue abandonment notice unless deficiency corrected and extension under §1.136 obtained. The six-month statutory max and five-month extension limits apply to extensions under §1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations causing abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated situations that often raise abandonment questions include: (A) copying claims from a patent (not a response), (B) withdrawal/failure to prosecute appeals, (C) dismissal of appeals/civil actions without filing responsive amendment, (D) interference claim suggestions near end of reply period, (E) FWC applications under former §1.62, (F) filing a continued prosecution application (CPA) under §1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP cross-references. Examiners and practitioners should be aware of these circumstances when determining abandonment and appropriate remedial action or petitioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings for copendency (35 U.S.C. 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings on an earlier application are terminated upon patenting, abandonment, or termination of proceedings on the earlier application; 'before' in this context is interpreted as 'not later than'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failure to pay issue fee leading to abandonment terminates proceedings as of the due date; revival changes status (see petition practice). See MPEP §711.03(c) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of a holding of abandonment by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may ask for reconsideration of a holding of abandonment if they dispute whether abandonment occurred (e.g., dispute as to sufficiency of reply or dates); an examiner may reverse a prior holding if convinced the case was never abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration differs from revival: if examiner treats an amendment received during the reply period as responsive, examiner may act on the case as never abandoned. See MPEP §714.03 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment (37 CFR 1.181) vs petition to revive (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant contends the application is not in fact abandoned (dispute as to sufficiency or dates), file a petition under §1.181 requesting withdrawal of the holding of abandonment (no fee). If there is no dispute the application is abandoned (disagreement only as to cause), file a petition to revive under §1.137 (fee required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A §1.181 petition must generally be filed within two months of the action complained of or may be dismissed as untimely under §1.181(f). Filing a petition does not stay the period for reply or other proceedings unless specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing required to establish nonreceipt of an Office action (petition to withdraw holding)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish nonreceipt, the practitioner must state the Office communication was not received, attest a search of the file jacket and docket records indicates nonreceipt, and attach a copy of the docket report where the nonreceived action would have been entered (e.g., showing replies docketed for a date three months from the mail date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing may be insufficient if circumstances suggest the action was lost after receipt or a history of not receiving Office actions exists. Evidence of nonreceipt of communications other than the action to which reply was required will not warrant withdrawal of the holding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of abandoned application—grounds and required elements (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revival may be sought under §1.137(a) for unavoidable delay or §1.137(b) for unintentional delay. Each grantable petition must include the required reply, the applicable petition fee (§1.17(l) or §1.17(m)), the required showing (entire delay was unavoidable or a statement the entire delay was unintentional), and any terminal disclaimer required by §1.137(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may require additional information where delay characterization is in doubt. Revival petitions differ in fees and standard of proof between unavoidable and unintentional categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement for revival (37 CFR 1.137(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications, utility applications filed before June 8, 1995, or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, petitions to revive must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer dedicating to the public a terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment. Special terminal disclaimer rules also apply for untimely petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer must apply to any patent granted on continuing applications that claim priority under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c). Terminal disclaimers are not required under §1.137(c) for relief under some other circumstances (see MPEP discussion), but may be required for treating untimely petitions on the merits per §1.183.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for seeking reconsideration or review of refusal to revive
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive must be filed within two months of the decision (unless the decision states otherwise); this time period may be extended under §1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of short statutory/administrative deadlines for timely follow-up; extensions are possible under §1.136 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival limits for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application abandoned for failure to timely respond to an Office requirement may be revived under §1.137 but will be considered pending for no longer than twelve months from its filing date; under no circumstances will a provisional be regarded pending after twelve months from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional revival only preserves the application for the limited statutory provisional pendency period.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes the 'required reply' for revival petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The required reply depends on the reason for abandonment: for failure to pay the issue fee the required reply is payment of the issue fee (or outstanding balance); for nonprovisional prosecution failures, a reply to a non-final action may be an argument or amendment under §1.111, while for final actions the reply must cancel/appeal each rejected claim or be a continuing application; for abandonment due to missing appeal brief, the reply must be the appeal brief or a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application is a permissible reply in many circumstances and may be required by the Office where acceptance of a reply under §1.111/1.113 would place an inordinate burden on the Office (e.g., inordinate period of abandonment, multiple/conflicting replies, questionable compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office review of amendments filed as the required reply after final action
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proposed amendment under §1.116 is filed as the required reply in a case abandoned after a final action, the amendment will normally be routed to the examining group to determine whether it places the application in condition for allowance prior to granting revival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner finds the reply places the application in condition for allowance, examiner should annotate 'OK to enter upon revival'; if not, examiner should complete form PTOL-303 and return the unmailed form to the Office of Petitions with the application. A petition will be granted only if the reply places the application in condition for allowance and other petition requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Office may treat an untimely §1.181 petition on the merits and terminal disclaimer conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An untimely petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment under §1.181(f) may, at the Office's discretion, be treated on the merits provided that (for certain application types and filing dates) it is accompanied by an appropriate terminal disclaimer dedicating patent term equivalent to the period between the notice of abandonment mail date and the petition filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For utility or plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995, treatment on the merits may be conditioned on a terminal disclaimer covering any patent term that would extend beyond 20 years from the relevant filing date. The Office may simply dismiss petitions showing intentional delay.
